cells.tense: Right now you are the place where what arrives becomes a choice, not a wave.
cells.act: close the cycle and leave the door open for the next
cells.ask: Take something you have been carrying toward its end and close it — mark it done in whatever way fits. Let whatever comes next stay unhurried. It can start when it starts.
cells.core:
You can watch a pattern move without flinching, and still be standing in the middle of it as it turns. That is rarer than it sounds. Most people get carried. You get to meet. Where this is going well, what arrives is not a wave that knocks you sideways — it is the next turn, and you are already on your feet for it. You do not have to decide who you are about it; you get to be at the hinge.

The risk is not watching too little. It is that the fresh entry stops feeling like one — you lean on the next turn instead of the one happening now, and the doorway becomes something you stand in front of rather than cross. So find what is finishing near you, a project, a habit, a season, and finish it deliberately. Leave the next thing unwritten. That closing is what keeps the entry fresh.

cells.tense: The next arrival is already pulling at you, and you are leaning toward it before it has come.
cells.act: complete it without making it final
cells.ask: Finish what is nearly done — the last actual step of it. Then do not reopen it, do not hand it forward. It is complete as it is, and the next thing can wait.
cells.core:
When this runs hot, the turning point stops being a place you stand and becomes something you are carried by. The next arrival feels decided already — some outcome, some change you can feel coming — and you are braced for it, planning around it, doing its work before it is here. What is underneath stays invisible; the cause of things keeps landing somewhere other than you. The choice got dropped, and what is left is momentum.

Finishing something actual brings you back. Not someday-finished — the last real step of a real thing, done and set down without being made final. One cycle closed, the next not yet begun. When you stop holding total responsibility for what has not arrived, the shape of the present returns. You are not managing the turn; you are entering it.

cells.tense: You were at the hinge of something once, and you are at the doorway with the choice already behind you.
cells.act: let the finished thing be the start of something
cells.ask: Look at what already finished — a season, a job, a way of being carried — and say what it made possible. Then take one small step in the direction it opened. No plan, just the step.
cells.core:
When this runs empty, the person at the turning looks like someone standing beside it. Something ended and was not marked ended. The current asked to move through and the feet stayed planted. There may be whole practices built around not agreeing to enter — and none of them are the trouble here. The trouble is one hinge, and it is behind you.

Effort will not solve this. But energy put toward the closing — one finished stretch being recognised as finished — pulls the current back into the starved pattern. So go find what already completed, name what it opened, and take one step in that opening's direction. Not a leap. One step. A finished thing is allowed to start another.

cells.tense: The wheel is already moving and you have not noticed that your hand is on it.
cells.act: set a direction and take the first step in it
cells.ask: Recall a moment this week that surprised you, and find your own move in it — a choice you made, or did not — and put it in a note. Nothing more. No conclusion.
cells.core:
You do not yet see the pattern you are in. That is what this looks like from here. Things arrive and land, and afterwards the landing looks like something outside you that chose. The cause is somewhere else. The cycles keep cycling. The consequences come as surprise, even the ones you saw coming.

What returns this is a smaller question than the big ones. Not what is the pattern, not who you really are — but which choice, exactly, was yours in one moment this week. Point attention at one happening, find the one move you made or did not, and put it in a note. Nothing grand. The direction that comes back here is chosen on purpose, from what is actually present, not from the wheel's momentum. You pick the one step. That is the first thing.
